name: 99 (trick-taking)
description: Ninety-Nine: trick-taking with exact-trick bidding. Bid by discarding 3 cards (Clubs=3, Hearts=2, Spades=1, Diamonds=0). 3-4 players; 36 or 52 cards. Follow suit; score for making exact bid and premiums for face-up or revealed hand. Designed by David Parlett 1967-68.

history.origins: Invented by David Parlett (1967-68). Trick-taking with exact-trick bidding via discard (suit = trick value). Distinct from adding game 99.
timeline: 1967-1968: David Parlett develops Ninety-Nine as a three-player trick-taking game with exact-trick bidding by discard.
1975: The rules for Ninety-Nine are first published in card game collections.
1990: Parlett revises the rules, establishing the modern version of Ninety-Nine.
Late 20th century: Ninety-Nine appears in card-game books in countries such as Germany, Hungary, Japan, and Argentina.

rules.objective: Score points by making exactly your bid (tricks bid via discard: Clubs=3, Hearts=2, Spades=1, Diamonds=0).
rules.gameplay: Discard 3 cards to bid (sum of suit values = trick bid). Play with remaining cards; follow suit. Make exact bid to score; premiums for face-up or revealed hand.

variations.name: Ninety-Nine for three players (standard game)
variations.description: Base Ninety-Nine uses a 36-card French-suited pack, deals 12 cards to each of three players, and has everyone discard three bid cards whose suits encode an exact trick target.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Standard three-player rules are fully described in the main rules; no separate engine overrides are modeled for this entry.

variations.name: Ninety-Nine for four players
variations.description: Four-player Ninety-Nine uses a full 52-card deck, deals 13 cards each, and allows bids up to 10 tricks, with three diamonds representing either 0 or 10 tricks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Four-player scoring and deal changes are rules-level variations; engine overrides for this mode have not yet been modeled.

variations.name: Ninety-Nine for five players
variations.description: Five-player Ninety-Nine uses a Five Hundred style pack including elevens and twelves, with each player discarding three bid cards to aim for up to nine tricks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Five-player seating, deck, and scoring adjustments are documented in rules but engine overrides are not yet specified.

variations.name: Two-player Ninety-Nine with dummy
variations.description: In the two-player variant a third dummy hand is dealt, its three bid cards are set aside unseen, and the live players both bid and may declare while also playing cards from the dummy hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dummy-hand flow and scoring follow the narrative rules; engine overrides for this two-player mode are still to be added.

variations.name: Original Ninety-Nine with joker
variations.description: The original three-player version adds a joker to the 36-card pack, uses the turn-up card to set trumps, and plays a fixed rubber of nine deals.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This legacy version changes deck and trump selection but not core engine structure; overrides can be added later if needed.

variations.name: Declarer chooses trumps
variations.description: In this variation a player who declares or reveals also chooses the trump suit for the deal instead of using the usual success-based trump rotation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Trump-choice timing alters game flow but reuses the same trick-taking engine; specific overrides are left for future modeling.

variations.name: Unbidden Ninety-Nine
variations.description: Unbidden Ninety-Nine delays bidding until the final three cards of each hand, using those cards as the bid while players have already played nine tricks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Late-bid timing and premium variants are described in rules; engine overrides for this mode are not yet implemented.

scoring.description: Points for making exact bid; bonuses for declarations. First to target wins.
